title: Book One · Chapter 137: The Door with No Name
story:
Leo's street game has six doors. People will look at a drawing and read a clue. The clue will help them find a door. They must choose the right door on the map.

He brings it to school in a paper cover. Ronan opens it carefully. Mei looks over his shoulder.

“Whose doors?” she asks.

“Places on River Street.”

“They all look like my aunt's door.”

Leo studies them. He has made six little squares. All have round handles on the same side.

“They are very good doors.”

“They are the same door.”

Ronan points to the green one. “Our gate has two parts.”

Leo gives him the pencil. “Then fix your gate.”

Ronan draws the line down the middle. He makes the top a little higher. It begins to look like home. Then Mei points to a small grey door in the corner.

“This one has no name.”

“I forgot,” Leo says.

Ronan knows the place. It is a narrow closed shop between two busy ones. There are no goods in its window now. He often walks past it. But he does not know the people inside.

“We can find out,” he says.

After school they ask Mum to walk that way. Mei comes too, because she wants to look at the window shapes. She carries her own small book and does not let either boy draw in it.

The grey door is shut. There is a plain notice inside the glass. Mum reads it. No one is working there now. Someone new may use it later.

“Then it is an empty shop,” Ronan says.

“For now,” Mum says.

Mei draws the long window and the short step. A woman from the next shop comes out with a broom. She sees them looking.

“Are you waiting for someone?”

Mum explains about the map. The woman says the shop used to sell bowls. Ronan remembers a blue bowl in the window when he was smaller. Now he can remember that bowl. He forgot that bowl for a long time. The woman's words help him remember it.

Leo wants to write OLD BOWL SHOP at once. Mum asks him to wait. The woman remembers a shop selling bowls. That is all she has told them. But they do not know the shop's real name. They cannot write one on the card yet.

“Could we leave it grey?” Mei asks. “We do not know this place yet.”

Ronan looks at the closed door. He wishes they knew more about it. But he does not want to guess an answer.

On the walk back Mei stops at a window with old bowls still for sale. None is blue. She draws the long shelf anyway. “Are you making our whole game again?” Leo asks. She shakes her head. These are drawings for her own book. Ronan looks at her page only when she holds it out for him. He finds the grey door at its edge.

At home they add a blank card to the game. The question on it is simple: WHAT WAS HERE BEFORE?

Under it Leo writes: DO YOU KNOW? PLEASE TELL US.

“It has no answer,” Ronan says.

“It has a job.”

They laugh. Mei draws a little open book on the card. She agrees to let them use that drawing for the game if they keep her name beside it.

When Miss Wu sees the blank door, she does not fill it in. She asks them to keep a space for new answers too. Leo cuts three more plain cards. They can leave the answer blank for now. A visitor may have an answer for the children.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：clue＝提示；blank＝空白的；for now＝目前。

情节提示：notice＝告示；broom＝扫帚；goods＝商品。

理解：1. 三个人为什么去看灰色店门？2. 为什么最后保留了一张没有确定答案的卡？
